sentences.text: By the team's ranking, the investigations closest to a cotton fabric in a lunar base are SAFFIRE-II (PSI-99), SAFFIRE-I (PSI-98) and ACME BRE (PSI-20).
Solid-fuel tests in the team's tables record the oxygen of the surrounding atmosphere for 139 of 376 tests, from 13.6 to 22.2%, so the 30% of this environment is above the highest recorded value.
Solid-fuel tests record pressure for 0 of 376 tests, so the 70.3 kPa of this environment is not comparable with a recorded value.

For extinction conditions, 17 of the 298 counted tests were recorded with oxygen and pressure both inside this environment's ranges, while none of the 133 tests counted for the flammability limit was.

facts.text: Closest to this input by the team's ranking, in order: SAFFIRE-II (PSI-99), SAFFIRE-I (PSI-98), ACME BRE (PSI-20).
SAFFIRE-II (PSI-99): closest configuration SIBAL fabric (0.37 mm), concurrent 20 cm/s; fuel match 1.00 (fuel SIBAL (75% cotton, 25% fiberglass)); flow match 0.90 (flow concurrent at 20 cm/s).

SAFFIRE-I (PSI-98): closest configuration Large SIBAL fabric (0.94 x 0.4 m), concurrent flow 20 cm/s; fuel match 1.00 (fuel SIBAL (75% cotton, 25% fiberglass)); flow match 0.90 (flow concurrent at 20 cm/s).

ACME BRE (PSI-20): closest configuration Porous gas burner emulating a burning solid, quiescent ambient; O2 match 1.00 (O2 tested 21–40%); fuel match 0.50 (fuel methane; ethylene (100% or 50% in N2)).
SAFFIRE-II (PSI-99): O2 0.24 (O2 tested 22.1%).
SAFFIRE-I (PSI-98): O2 0.22 (O2 tested 21.5–21.7%).
ACME BRE (PSI-20): sample shape 0.20 (porous_burner (regime n/a)).

PSI has no partial-gravity (lunar or Martian) combustion data. All results here are microgravity tests; they are not bounds for lunar or Martian gravity. NASA names partial-gravity material flammability a major gap (OCHMO-TB-008).
The ranking is the team's similarity score over the catalog, not NASA's conclusion and not a fire-safety judgement.
